elements.text: 3. WHY SOME THINGS ARE HARD TO FIX (the real reasons)

Every free avenue has been exhausted: African Financials (the source that works for Nigeria/Kenya) has zero South African or Egyptian companies - their sitemap lists 632 companies, none from ZA or EG. Yahoo's fundamentals API requires a paid subscription (returns 401). Company IR websites host the statements, but as scanned image PDFs that have no text layer - text extraction returns empty. The only paths to real JSE/EGX numbers are: (a) OCR on ~800 scanned annual reports (hours of compute, imperfect accuracy), or (b) a licensed feed (Twelve Data ~$8/month gives clean structured income statements for all 805).

Many annual reports are published as image-only PDFs. pypdf's text extraction returns empty strings for them because there is no text layer - the pages are photographs of the printed report. Parsing numbers from images requires OCR (tesseract/paddleOCR), which is heavy: roughly 30-60 seconds per 100-page report, with accuracy that degrades on dense financial tables. This is why the IR crawl yields ~2%: of 50 JSE companies tried, 34 had no discoverable website, 6 no IR page, and of the ones with PDFs, most were scans.

Finding each company's IR site requires either a search engine (DuckDuckGo blocks bulk queries from this IP), Wikipedia (rate-limits at 429 after ~50 requests, and small caps have no article), or a curated directory (the JSE website is JavaScript-rendered with no crawlable company list; Twelve Data's free API provides no website field). The liquid top-200 names are discoverable; the long tail of small caps is not.

Uchumi, Mumias, WAPCO/Lafarge, Dunlop, Aradel and preference shares like KPLC-P4 simply do not trade. No free feed carries quotes for securities that are delisted or suspended. No software fix changes this - the market itself does not produce the data.

Yahoo dropped Kenyan/Nigerian tickers (returns 404 or wrong US instruments). Real intraday history does not exist on any free source for these exchanges. The terminal now shows honest EOD-derived 6-point history from kwayisi period returns (1W/1M/3M/6M/1Y/YTD) - real published returns, not fabricated data. True minute-level candles require a licensed exchange feed.

Everything that free data can deliver is delivered and verified: 1,030 stocks, live prices on 767 securities, real sector heatmaps, honest NSE/NGX history, 176 company financial statements, 128 shareholder breakdowns, 190 descriptions, and a 70-field metrics suite. The remaining gaps - JSE/EGX statements (805 companies), 22 unpriced securities, and intraday history - are blocked by data availability, not by effort. They close with either OCR (free but slow and imperfect) or a $8/month data key (instant, clean, complete). No number in this report is invented, and no failure is hidden.
